subject: Re: Performance SLOs & Private VPC network follow-up (Acme Corp)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam@acme.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 25 May 2027 15:34:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap: Performance SLOs & private VPC checklist

Hi Liam,

Thanks again for taking the call earlier — good to align on Acme's performance goals. Below is a concise recap and proposed next steps so we can validate whether Redwood Private in a VPC/peered setup will meet your SLOs.

Key SLOs you mentioned:
- Target p95 latency (inference): <= 100 ms (end-to-end)
- Target throughput: ~200 requests/sec steady state, with spikes to 400 req/sec for short bursts
- Concurrency target: ~50 concurrent active sessions
- Streaming support: yes (server-sent partial tokens; must keep tail latency under 250 ms)

Private/VPC constraints to validate:
- Primary deployment: Acme VPC in us-west-2 with peering to Redwood Private VPC (or site-to-site VPN for on-prem component)
- Expected egress path: outbound through Acme NAT gateway into internet for model downloads and optional external telemetry; prefer peering if possible to avoid NAT egress overhead
- Internal latency budget: 30-50 ms for VPC-peered path (round-trip) to keep overall inference p95 <= 100 ms
- MTU / fragmentation: ensure 1500 across VPN/peering; any lower MTU will affect streaming performance

What we need from Acme (next items to validate in a short tech pass / lab):
1) Network traces: traceroute/mtr from your inference hosts to our proposed peering IP (we provided a sample earlier).
2) VPN/peering contact & config: who manages peering or VPN (PSIRT/SRE contact) + proposed CIDR blocks.
3) Egress profile: whether NAT gateway introduces additional egress hops (and expected extra ms).
4) Expected steady-state CPU/GPU concurrency per instance and whether you have sidecar proxies that add latency.
5) Optional: a short synthetic test plan (5-minute steady load at 200 req/s) we can run together.

Attached: SLO_requirements.xlsx (spreadsheet we discussed with our suggested perf thresholds).

Proposed next steps:
- If you can share traceroutes and the SRE contact, Jordan will spin up a short lab to validate peering vs VPN paths and measure tail latency under streaming.
- Schedule a 30-min lab review next week (I’m proposing Wed 2 Jun 10:30am PT).

Thanks — will be ready to run the lab as soon as we have the network artifacts.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.ai
(415) 555-0139

Attachments: SLO_requirements.xlsx

From: Liam O'Connor <liam@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Cc: SRE Team <sre@acme.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 26 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: Performance SLOs & private VPC checklist

Thanks Marissa — great summary. A few clarifications and I attached our network diagram + recent traces.

Notes on our side:
- Our inference hosts will live in a private subnet in us-west-2 behind a NAT gateway; we prefer VPC peering but have limited peering capacity in our current account (we can open a ticket to request an additional peering connection).
- Egress: NAT adds ~5-10 ms on average according to our monitoring — SRE flagged that as the main variability source.
- Streaming: we use a small envoy sidecar; typical additional latency per request is ~3-6 ms but tail can spike during scale-ups.

Attached: acme_vpc_diagram.png, net-traces-20270520.zip (contains traceroute + ping samples).

SRE contact: Priya Natarajan (priya@acme.com) — she owns peering/VPN and will coordinate the ticket.

We’re happy to run the synthetic test but would like Redwood to provide a config (endpoint IPs, test payload, expected token sizes) so we can align on load generation. If Wed 2 Jun 10:30am PT works, I’ll add Priya and our SRE on the invite.

—Liam
Liam O'Connor
Senior Product Manager, Acme Corp
liam@acme.com

Attachments: acme_vpc_diagram.png, net-traces-20270520.zip

From: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 27 May 2027 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: Prep for Acme lab run (confidential)

Marissa / Laura,

Quick internal plan before the lab run with Acme:
- I will provision a dedicated Redwood Private staging instance in us-west-2 with the same model config they plan to use (quantization Q4_NV and streaming enabled).
- Run two profiles: peered path (simulate peering by colocating in same AZ) and NAT path (route via a NAT gateway to reproduce +5-10 ms).
- Measurement targets: p50/p95/p99 for end-to-end token latency, connection setup time, and streaming tail latency. Collect histograms and sample traces (jaeger).
- Checklist for test config to send to Acme: endpoint IPs, TLS cert fingerprint, test payload size (we should mirror their average token size they shared), and step-by-step load script (wrk + custom streaming client).

I’ll prepare the config by Monday 31 May and share the test harness link. After the synthetic run, we can propose a canary rollout plan: start with 10% traffic, monitor p95, then 50% -> 100% if stable.

Jordan
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Subject: RE: Post-call recap: Performance SLOs & private VPC checklist

Hi Liam / Priya,

Thanks for the quick reply and for sharing the diagrams/traces. Wed 2 Jun 10:30am PT works for us — I’ve tentatively booked 30 minutes.

Prior to the call, please share:
- Final traceroute/mtr outputs from your intended inference hosts to this IP: 34.201.122.87 (we’ll use that for peering proof-of-concept).
- Any firewall rules (NSG) that might block inbound traffic from Redwood.
- A contact for the VPN/peering ticket (Priya noted she will own this) + desired CIDR for peering.

Jordan will send the test harness and endpoint details by EOD Mon 31 May. During the 2 Jun session we’ll:
1) Run the short synthetic test (5 min at 200 req/s) over both peering and NAT paths.
2) Review p95/p99 tail behavior (streaming tail latency is our primary SLO risk).
3) Confirm a canary rollout cadence and fallback options.

If we see NAT-induced variability in the lab, recommended mitigations:
- Move to VPC peering (preferred) or enable a direct connect/VPN to reduce hops.
- Increase keepalive tuning on envoy and ensure MTU consistent across path.

Link to the checklist & docs: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1a2B3cSLO-checklist

Looking forward to the run — see you Wed.

Best,
